correctness.rationale: Exact finite-dimensional π2/Pietsch minimax converts the unrestricted free-lattice norm into a positive-semidefinite trace-root design. The S_a × S_b orbit spectrum has eigenvalues ((1-u)/a+2t²u/(a-1), (1-u)/b, (a+b)(1-u)/(ab)) with multiplicities (a-1,b-1,1). The strictly concave scalar maximization, derivative at u=0, and Cauchy equality give the two exact branches and a matching boundary. A global supporting hyperplane provides simultaneous iff screening for arbitrary clique-edge subsets and amplitudes. Differentiation and explicit asymptotics are reproduced in the mathematical proof; local checker passes 58 configurations, supplementary not infinite proof. Quantifiers: real H=ℓ₂^(a+b), a≥3, b≥2, t≥0.

value.rationale: The sharp exact π2 norm on the natural family K_a joined to an independent b-set has an amplitude plateau, a nontrivial post-threshold algebraic branch, and a simultaneous iff criterion for arbitrary individual clique-edge amplitudes; these cannot be derived from bare spectral enumeration without optimizing the design. The screening amplitude grows as (b/a)^(1/4)/√2 while the positive lattice element can grow pointwise, and the norm has an exact strictly positive curvature jump. These are motivated structural operator-ideal invariants for infinite graph families, not arbitrary finite slices.
